newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH-U.S. COMPANY GETS TELEVISION LICENCE.
newsitem.headline: POLISH-U.S. COMPANY GETS TELEVISION LICENCE.

text.p: Poland's electronic media authority awarded a regional television operation licence on Tuesday to a joint venture of local firm ITI TV Holdings and U.S.-based Central European Media Enterprises .

The venture, called TVN, said in a statement that the National Radio and Television Council (KRRiT) had awarded it a licence to use frequencies in Poland's nine northern provinces and in the large urban areas of Warsaw and Lodz.

TVN, in which Central European Media Enterprises has 33 percent and ITI holds the remaining shares, said it plans to invest up to $150 million over the next three years to develop the television service.
It said TVN -- which also holds a 49 percent stake in TV Wisla, a company broadcasting in southern Poland -- should reach up to 85 percent of Polish households within three years.
TVN will rival Poland's two nationwide public television channels, the sole private nationwide television broadcaster Polsat and numerous stations available on cable and satellites.
